name: team_planning_cost
description: Get what a scenario of a Team Planning plan the caller is in costs over its period, beside the baseline priced over the same days, with the difference. Each seat (a person, or the FTE a position's occupants leave open) is priced at the midpoint of its pay band: of the tenant's pay bands that match the seat's role family, role, level number and location each band sets, or a framework level's level_id and location, the last in tenants_pay_bands order. The midpoint is made yearly (a month is 1/12, an hour takes the working_hours rule), scaled by FTE and by the days it is held out of the year (365, or the run rate's own year: 366 across a 29 February), plus the on_cost rule of its unit. A person is priced at their own level, a planned one winning, and at their position's level only when theirs resolves to none; level_source says which. A leaver costs up to their leaving date and their backfill from the day after. Totals are per currency in `native`, and `converted` is the same in the reference currency at the period's start, null with `missing` saying why when a rate is missing. Units count their own places, with null for no unit; `with_below` adds the units below. Cost centres use null for no cost centre. A person keeps their own cost centre unless the plan changes their unit or the units above it, role, level or location (an FTE change alone doesn't). A changed person, or a real person with none, takes their position's own cost centre, else the last entry of the cost_centre rule at their unit that matches their planned unit, role or role family, level number and location, else their own, else none. An open seat takes its position's own cost centre, else an unchanged occupant's, else the last matching entry read at its largest occupant's country (an empty seat has none), else none; a placeholder hire in a position reads as that open seat. A seat's cost_centre_source says which (position, person, rule or none); for a rule, cost_centre_rule is the entry's index in the list that unit reads and cost_centre_matcher is what it matches on. Unit, cost-centre and plan totals always agree. Every total carries `parts`, which add up to its `scenario` figure exactly. In `parts`, actual means the baseline's figure, not actual pay: actual is the baseline's figure for the same unit or cost centre over the same days, planned is what the plan's changes add or take away (negative where they take away, so someone moved between units is negative in the old unit and positive in the new), and forecast is what the plan's forecast assumptions add, zero until a forecast rule is set; team_planning_forecast lists its rows. A run rate is all actual. A seat that can't be priced is in `unpriced` with its reason, never counted as zero. Pass unit_id for the working of each seat in that unit. Plans reprice live: bands_changed_at says when a band last changed. Bands are an ordered list (tenants_pay_bands); each matches on the role family, role, level number and location it sets, or on a framework level's level_id and location, and of the bands that match a seat the last in the list has the last word. Each seat's band names its position in the list and its matcher. Pass the plan's id as scenario_id for Today's run rate: basis is run_rate, period is the year from the base date to the day before the same date a year later, each seat is priced for that whole year, and totals carry only `scenario`, with no baseline or difference, as a run rate is never compared with a period total. A scenario has basis period. A scenario also has run_rate_at_end: every seat it holds on its last day (`on`), each priced for a full year and converted at that day's rates, beside the baseline's seats priced the same way, so a move in exchange rates is never a planned change. Its difference is on Today's run rate. Its parts: actual is the baseline on that day, planned what the plan's changes add or take away, and forecast a year of each forecast row's headcount still changed that day, at the row's average cost (for attrition, the steady share of seats waiting to be filled). For a step with no end date, `on` is the last day of the months shown, and open_ended and horizon_months say so. Today has none, as it is a run rate already. pay_view is band_ranges for a member with the see-pay right, whose working shows each band's minimum and maximum, and band_midpoints for everyone else. For a holder, a person whose actual pay the plan holds is priced from it instead (made yearly, scaled by FTE only when its basis is full_time, by the days held, plus on-cost), in a run rate as in a scenario: each seat's pay_source says actual or band_midpoint, and actual_pay_seats counts the seats priced from actual pay. Held pay the plan lost with the person's key leaves the seat unpriced as pay_unknown. Everyone else is priced at midpoints throughout, so the two views total differently. Figures are decimal strings; people are named by id in `names`. An archived plan carries archived_on and a note: its figures still use today's pay bands, exchange rates, budget lines and rules, not those of the day it was archived. A step with no end date runs, for its figures, over the plan's open_step_horizon rule in whole months from its start: its period's ends_on is that horizon's last day, with open_ended true and horizon_months the months shown. Otherwise open_ended is false and horizon_months null. Refused, as an unknown plan, unless the caller is a member.

scenario_id.description: A scenario of the plan, or the plan's id for Today's yearly run rate.

unit_id.description: A unit on the scenario's or the baseline's map, for the working of each seat in it.
